question: An investigator is studying the physiological response during congestive heart failure exacerbations in patients with systolic heart failure. A hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes in response to increased wall stress is isolated from a patient's blood sample. The intracellular mechanism by which this hormone acts is most similar to the effect of which of the following substances?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes -> response to increased wall stress -> similar intracellular mechanism to Angiotensin II -> 80% CHAIN: Hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes -> acts on the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system -> similar to Aldosterone effect -> 75% CHAIN: Hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes -> promotes vasoconstriction and sodium retention -> similar to Angiotensin II -> 70% CHAIN: Hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes -> involved in fluid and electrolyte balance regulation -> similar to Aldosterone -> 80%
analysis: The hormone released by ventricular cardiomyocytes in response to increased wall stress is likely to be B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP). BNP is released in response to increased ventricular wall stress and volume overload. The intracellular mechanism of action of BNP is most similar to the effect of option d, Angiotensin II, as both hormones act on the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system to regulate blood pressure and fluid balance.
